title: 0-1 knapsack: optimal selection at capacity 50
summary: Selecting the weight-20 banana and weight-30 grapes from five items fills capacity 50 exactly for a maximum value of 270.
context: In 0-1 knapsack, each item may be chosen at most once to maximize total value without exceeding knapsack capacity. This example has 5 items and knapsack capacity cap = 50; item IDs i run from 1 to 5, mapping to array index i - 1 (written wgt[i - 1] and val[i - 1] in the figure's table header).
description: At the upper left, a table lists the icon, weight, and value of items 1 through 5 (full data in the table below); row 2 (banana) is shaded light orange and row 3 (grapes) is shaded light purple, each sending an arrow to the purple knapsack icon at the upper right labeled "Knapsack capacity cap = 50".
Below, the result box states "Maximum value: 270" and pairs the banana and grapes icons with "Optimal choice: pack [banana and grapes] into the knapsack using 50 units of capacity in total".

frames.title: 0-1 knapsack: optimal selection at capacity 50
frames.explanation: Computed from the input data, choosing item 2 (banana) and item 3 (grapes) gives total weight 20 + 30 = 50 and total value 120 + 150 = 270. That is the highest value among all non-overweight subsets—beating, for instance, 260 from items 1 and 4 or 240 from item 5 alone, supplied here from the input table for comparison.
